import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 45

Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$,
such that every integer $\leq N$ lies in at least 10 of them?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
- [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»`.
-/

findings.description: Lines 23–24 describe tenfold coverage, and line 30 identifies the imported Erdős 689 module as its canonical formalization. However, that module's only problem declaration, `Erdos689.erdos_689`, requires `2 ≤ (...).card`, not tenfold coverage. The reviewed file declares no additional theorem supplying the tenfold version. Thus the redirect inaccurately presents the related twofold question as the formalization of Green's stated question. The imported Erdős theorem itself correctly states its own source's twofold problem.
findings.source_evidence: Green, Problem 45, https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45, asks for every integer to lie in 'at least 10' classes; its comments explicitly say that Erdős could not answer the question 'with 10 replaced by 2.' https://www.erdosproblems.com/689 likewise explicitly identifies Green's problem as its question 'with 2 replaced by 10.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a separate tenfold variant here or in the canonical module, using the existing eventual-in-n statement with `10 ≤ (...).card`, and point the redirect to that variant. Alternatively, clarify that the imported module currently formalizes only the related twofold question. Keep the existing twofold Erdős declaration unchanged.

reformulations.difference: For the imported twofold problem, Lean chooses an unrestricted total function `a : ℕ → ℕ`, rather than explicitly choosing reduced residue representatives only for primes at most n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Replace each value by `a p % p`. For prime p this is less than p, and it leaves every congruence and hence every coverage count unchanged. Conversely, reduced representatives are also unrestricted natural representatives; choices outside the relevant primes can be extended arbitrarily. The scratch file proves the corresponding existential equivalence for every multiplicity k and bound n.
